rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biotechnology reshaped microbiology by turning bacteria into factories. Restriction enzymes cut, DNA ligase glues, plasmids and phages ship, and E. coli grows — recombinant DNA in five steps. The impacts: medicine gains human insulin, hepatitis B vaccine, interferons and antibiotics; agriculture gains Bt cotton, golden rice and Rhizobium biofertilisers; industry gains fermentation products, enzymes and single-cell…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
rDNA: isolate → cut (restriction enzyme) → ligate (DNA ligase) → transform → select → express → harvest
Plasmid: ori + selectable marker + MCS + high copy number
Insulin: human gene → E. coli → fermentation → purification → insulin

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Restriction enzyme vs ligase:** restriction endonuclease cuts DNA at specific sites; DNA ligase seals fragments together.  ·  **Vector vs host:** vector = the DNA carrier (plasmid/phage); host = the organism multiplied (E. coli).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the 7 rDNA steps clearly, with the role of each tool (restriction enzyme, ligase, vector, host).  ·  The plasmid vector structure (ori, selectable marker, MCS, copy number) is a common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Humulin*** — first rDNA drug (1982); human insulin from E. coli.  ·  ***Bt cotton*** — insect-resistant transgenic cotton.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Cut–Glue–Ship–Grow": cut (restriction), glue (ligase), ship (vector), grow (host).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Q.** What is PCR? **Answer.** **Polymerase Chain Reaction**: in vitro enzymatic amplification of a chosen DNA segment through repeated cycles of heat denaturation, primer annealing and extension by thermostable *Taq* polymerase.…

rows.text: Most-tested in exams: recombinant DNA steps, named products (insulin, vaccine), Bt crops, bioremediation.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One enzyme, one cut:** the same restriction enzyme cutting both gene and vector creates matching sticky ends — the molecular hinge of all genetic engineering.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Tools: restriction enzymes (EcoRI), DNA ligase, plasmid/phage vectors, E. coli host, PCR (Taq polymerase), gel electrophoresis.  ·  rDNA steps: isolate gene → cut with same enzyme → ligate → transform host → select and express.  ·  Medicine: Humulin insulin (E. coli, 1982), hepatitis B vaccine (yeast), antibiotics (Streptomyces), interferons.  ·  Agriculture: Bt cotton/maize, golden rice, Rhizobium biofertiliser, biopesticides.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: PCR can amplify a single DNA molecule to billions of copies in about two hours.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Pseudomonas putida*** — oil-eating "superbug" of bioremediation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: CRISPR: guide RNA + Cas9 → cut DNA → repair → desired change  ·  Environment: sewage treatment, bioremediation (Pseudomonas putida oil spills), biogas (methanogens).  ·  **Bt gene vs Bt spray:** same Bacillus thuringiensis toxin — engineered into crops (Bt cotton) or sprayed as biopesticide.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The insulin production pathway (gene → E. coli → fermentation → purification) is a very frequent application question.  ·  Gene therapy vs gene editing (CRISPR): know the distinction.  ·  Bt crops: mechanism of insect resistance + one environmental concern.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ethical issues of GMOs: environmental, health, and social dimensions.  ·  Monoclonal antibodies: single B-cell clone; highly specific; diagnostics + therapy.  ·  Pay attention to key terminology in Biotechnology in Microbiology.
